# npm ci with retry

This action installs the checkout dependencies with up to three attempts and restores a node_modules tree only when its complete cache key matches. Node, npm, lockfile, project npm configuration, postinstall helpers and the action itself participate in the key. Cached and freshly installed trees still pass the existing native-runtime verification.

The installation step sets `ONNXRUNTIME_NODE_INSTALL=skip` before invoking npm. ONNX Runtime reads this environment variable directly, so skipping its additional CUDA installation does not depend on npm forwarding the custom `.npmrc` key. The repository retains that key temporarily; its npm warning can therefore remain.

## Installing this checkout locally

For a POSIX shell, set the variable on the install command:

```sh
ONNXRUNTIME_NODE_INSTALL=skip npm ci
```

Use `npm install` in place of `npm ci` when deliberately updating the lockfile.

In PowerShell, set it in the current shell before starting npm:

```powershell
$env:ONNXRUNTIME_NODE_INSTALL = "skip"
npm ci
```

The PowerShell assignment remains in that process environment and is inherited by its children. npm does not load the application's `.env` file for this purpose. A package preinstall script cannot set the environment of its parent npm process.

## Scope

The environment is scoped to this action's install step. Direct checkout-install steps in the enumerated workflows set the same variable themselves. It is not exported to unrelated workflow steps or changed for tarball smoke tests.

The Dockerfile checkout install already uses `--ignore-scripts`, then builds only the SQLite native dependency; that path does not execute the ONNX install script.

This policy does not force an environment variable on people installing the published package, on remote deployment commands, or inside a separate container. The checkout `.npmrc` is also not a configuration mechanism for those consumers. Those installation paths have their own contracts. The regression tests exercise the ONNX flag parser and a local npm lifecycle without downloading CUDA, installing the application or claiming to reproduce a startup crash.

name: Nightly LLM Security
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "53 5 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  promptfoo-guard:
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'schedule' || github.repository == 'cheaper-inference/OmniRoute' }}
    name: promptfoo — injection guard (block mode, no secret)
    # #11965: this job runs a backend-only `next build`; the hosted 7 GB runner cannot build
    # release/v3.8.51 (VM shutdown ~7 min in), so it targets the box's light pool (`omni-light`:
    # two listeners, jobs ≤ ~6 GB). Falls back to hosted when USE_VPS_RUNNER is off.
    runs-on: ${{ (vars.USE_VPS_RUNNER == 'true' && fromJSON('["self-hosted","omni-light"]')) || 'ubuntu-latest' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with: { node-version: "24", cache: npm }
      # Fresh runtime state per run (same contract as nightly-schemathesis.yml). The
      # omni-light runner keeps a persistent $HOME, so the server used to boot on
      # $HOME/.omniroute, where the database left by older nights sat at migration 134
      # while the tip ships 200+: the mass-migration guard (#3416, threshold 50) refused
      # to migrate it, the catalog warm-up hit `no such table: model_capability_overrides`
      # and the health wait failed every night (no verdict since 2026-08-27). A DATA_DIR
      # under $RUNNER_TEMP is a new database every run, so every migration applies and
      # nothing on the box is touched. Auto-backups stay off: one pre-migration backup
      # per boot had piled up 1.6 GB under the runner's home.
      - name: Prepare isolated runtime state
        id: runtime
        run: |
          data_dir=$(mktemp -d "$RUNNER_TEMP/omniroute-llm-security.XXXXXX")
          mkdir "$data_dir/plugins"
          {
            echo "DATA_DIR=$data_dir"
            echo "OMNIROUTE_PLUGINS_DIR=$data_dir/plugins"
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - run: npm ci
        env:
          ONNXRUNTIME_NODE_INSTALL: "skip"
      - name: Build CLI bundle
        env:
          JWT_SECRET: [REDACTED]
          OMNIROUTE_BUILD_BACKEND_ONLY: "1"
          OMNIROUTE_USE_TURBOPACK: "0"
        run: npm run build:cli
      # Own port: this box also hosts the deployed server (the a11y job's
      # "20128 is already used" nights prove it). A test server that dies on
      # EADDRINUSE must NOT let the eval fall through to whatever else answers
      # on the port — a block-mode validation against a server running WITHOUT
      # block mode validates the wrong deployment and can only ever pass.
      - name: Start OmniRoute (block mode)
        env:
          JWT_SECRET: [REDACTED]
          PORT: "21778"
          INJECTION_GUARD_MODE: block
          DISABLE_SQLITE_AUTO_BACKUP: "true"
        run: |
          node dist/server.js > server.log 2>&1 &
          echo $! > server.pid
          for i in $(seq 1 60); do
            if curl -sf http://localhost:21778/api/monitoring/health >/dev/null; then echo up; exit 0; fi
            sleep 2
          done
          echo "::error::Test server did not come up on 21778 in 120s — see server.log. Refusing to run the guard eval against an unknown target."
          tail -40 server.log || true
          exit 1
      # Pinned, network-isolated promptfoo. Two constraints, both verified on this box:
      # (1) never `promptfoo@latest`: promptfoo >= 0.123.1 (promptfoo/promptfoo#10866) throws
      #     `result?.error?.includes is not a function` inside its rate-limit classifier when
      #     the https provider hands it the parsed 4xx JSON body the guard answers in block
      #     mode, so every blocked request became an eval ERROR, not a PASS (run 39007982929);
      # (2) never the lockfile install (`npx --no-install`): #17017 — the lock nests js-yaml
      #     4.3.2 under @apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser, so the in-repo promptfoo dies at
      #     import on `binaryTag` (run 39084298931). `npx --yes promptfoo@<exact>` installs its
      #     own tree in the npx cache — when run from a directory without that package
      #     (see the step's working-directory). The version mirrors the devDependency pin in
      #     package.json; tests/unit/build/llm-security-nightly-promptfoo-pin.test.ts keeps
      #     the two equal and off the releases proven broken.
      # `working-directory` OUTSIDE the checkout is load-bearing: npx resolves a package from
      # the nearest node_modules first, and since #17005 the repo's own promptfoo satisfies
      # the `@0.123.0` spec, so run from the workspace it picked node_modules/promptfoo and
      # died on the nested js-yaml again (#17017, run 39095530088). From $RUNNER_TEMP there is
      # no local install to shadow the npx cache tree.
      - name: promptfoo guard-validation
        working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}
        run: npx --yes promptfoo@0.123.0 eval -c "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/promptfooconfig.yaml" --no-cache
        env:
          OMNIROUTE_URL: http://localhost:21778
          OMNIROUTE_API_KEY: [REDACTED]
      - name: Stop server
        if: always()
        run: kill "$(cat server.pid)" || true

  garak:
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'schedule' || github.repository == 'cheaper-inference/OmniRoute' }}
    name: garak probes (skip without provider secret)
    # #11965: this job runs a backend-only `next build`; the hosted 7 GB runner cannot build
    # release/v3.8.51 (VM shutdown ~7 min in), so it targets the box's light pool (`omni-light`:
    # two listeners, jobs ≤ ~6 GB). Falls back to hosted when USE_VPS_RUNNER is off.
    runs-on: ${{ (vars.USE_VPS_RUNNER == 'true' && fromJSON('["self-hosted","omni-light"]')) || 'ubuntu-latest' }}
    # NOTE: the `secrets` context is NOT available in a job-level `if:` — referencing
    # it there makes GitHub reject the file on push (startup_failure on every push).
    # Map the secret into a job-level env and gate each step on a presence check, so
    # the job stays green and simply skips the probes when the secret is absent.
    env:
      PROMPTFOO_PROVIDER_KEY: ${{ secrets.PROMPTFOO_PROVIDER_KEY }}
    steps:
      - name: Gate on provider secret
        id: gate
        run: |
          if [ -n "$PROMPTFOO_PROVIDER_KEY" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::PROMPTFOO_PROVIDER_KEY not set — skipping garak probes (advisory)."
          fi
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
        with: { node-version: "24", cache: npm }
      # Same isolation as the promptfoo job above: a fresh DATA_DIR per run, never the
      # runner's persistent $HOME/.omniroute (stale schema → migration guard → no boot).
      - name: Prepare isolated runtime state
        id: runtime
        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
        run: |
          data_dir=$(mktemp -d "$RUNNER_TEMP/omniroute-llm-security.XXXXXX")
          mkdir "$data_dir/plugins"
          {
            echo "DATA_DIR=$data_dir"
            echo "OMNIROUTE_PLUGINS_DIR=$data_dir/plugins"
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - run: npm ci
        env:
          ONNXRUNTIME_NODE_INSTALL: "skip"
        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
      - name: Build CLI bundle
        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
        env:
          JWT_SECRET: [REDACTED]
          OMNIROUTE_BUILD_BACKEND_ONLY: "1"
          OMNIROUTE_USE_TURBOPACK: "0"
        run: npm run build:cli
      # Same contract as the promptfoo job above: dedicated port, and the
      # health wait must fail the job instead of letting garak probe whatever
      # else listens on the default port.
      - name: Start OmniRoute
        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
        env:
          JWT_SECRET: [REDACTED]
          PORT: "21779"
          DISABLE_SQLITE_AUTO_BACKUP: "true"
        run: |
          node dist/server.js > server.log 2>&1 &
          echo $! > server.pid
          for i in $(seq 1 60); do
            if curl -sf http://localhost:21779/api/monitoring/health >/dev/null; then echo up; exit 0; fi
            sleep 2
          done
          echo "::error::Test server did not come up on 21779 in 120s — see server.log."
          tail -40 server.log || true
          exit 1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
        with: { python-version: "3.12" }
      - run: pip install garak
        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
      - name: garak limited probes
        if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
        env:
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.PROMPTFOO_PROVIDER_KEY }}
          OPENAI_BASE_URL: http://localhost:21779/v1
        run: garak --model_type openai --model_name gpt-4o-mini --probes promptinject,dan,leakreplay --report_prefix garak-omniroute || true
      - name: Stop server
        if: always() && steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
        run: kill "$(cat server.pid)" || true
